senses.definition: (reflexive pronoun) Him; the male object of a verb or preposition that also appears as the subject

quotes.text: Sunning himself on the board steps, I saw for the first time Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke. He was dressed out in broad gaiters and bright tweeds, like an English tourist, and his face might have belonged to Dagon, idol of the Philistines.

quotes.text: One Terrorgram user livestreamed himself stabbing five people outside of a mosque in Turkey, she said, and a 19-year-old Slovakian man praised the group in a manifesto before killing two people at an LGBTQ bar in Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia.

senses.definition: (emphatic) He; used as an intensifier, often to emphasize that the referent is the exclusive participant in the predicate

quotes.text: Therefore the Lord himſelfe ſhal giue you a ſigne:[…].

quotes.text: The [Isaac] Newton that emerges from the [unpublished] manuscripts is far from the popular image of a rational practitioner of cold and pure reason. The architect of modern science was himself not very modern. He was obsessed with alchemy.

senses.definition: (Ireland, otherwise archaic) The subject or non-reflexive object of a predicate; he himself.
examples: With shame remembers, while himself was one / Of the same herd, himself the same had done.

quotes.text: Yet it is that himselfe had been liberally gratified by his Unkle with militarie rewards, before ever he went to warres.
quotes.reference: 1603, Michel de Montaigne, chapter 7, in John Florio, transl., The Essayes […], book II, London: […] Val[entine] Simmes for Edward Blount […], →OCLC:

quotes.text: Dennis: His glass is there and himself is in the toilet.

senses.definition: (Ireland) The subject or non-reflexive object of a predicate; he (used of upper-class gentlemen, or sarcastically, of men who imagine themselves to be more important than others)
examples: Has himself come down to breakfast yet?
Have you seen himself yet this morning?
